I always have had to. If you can keep your humidity from getting to high maybe you won't have to. But see a lot of different soils that you buy at stores aren't very good and are full of various kinds of eggs and what not. If you buy properly composted soil you don't have to worry about that because the soil heating that occurs during composting kills most eggs and weed seeds.

The worst soil you can buy is miracle grow. So many times that shit has spawned swarms of fungus gnats..

You don't have to have a vermin problem but again you gotta do it right. High quality really good soil, high wattage lights, a good fan or dehumidifier to cut humidity and be really really careful with how much you water. I recommend not watering every day personally. I like to water every other day but sometimes that can cause problems too.

7 watt of cheap LED really would only be enough for one small plant and you'd need it almost touching, the diodes are probably very low individual wattage which means low penetration.

The outdoor temps are fine, my advice would be to keep the led but also grab some CFL's (or one big growing one), particularly in the warm white spectrum. This will have better coverage and increase your heat. Peppers will grow faster and hotter the closer to 90F you keep them.

I haven't used a double bucket setup, so can't help you with that one, but have had success with around 4 gallon containers and a soil mix of 5 parts Fir bark, 1 part perlite, 1 part potting soil mix and a 1/2 cup of dolomite lime per 4 gallon. This soil mix drains very quickly, so you will be watering frequently, but it's a hell of a lot faster growth than just potting mix.

Feed with seaweed, fish and worm juice in veg stage and then guano for flowering. Also, is good to stress the plants a bit if you want more heat and you think you have enough fruit formation.
Hand pollinate for nice big indoors peppers. I just use a q-tip.
